newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag expects approval for RWE stake swap.
newsitem.headline: Viag expects approval for RWE stake swap.

text.p: German energy concern Viag AG said on Tuesday it expects to win approval from the German cartel office for a swap of subsidiary holdings with RWE AG.
Viag's comments came after the European Commission referred earlier on Tuesday a plan by RWE Energy AG to take a 50 percent stake in Viag's Thyssengas GmbH unit.
"Viag continues to expect that the transaction will be brought to a successful conclusion in the near future," a company spokesman told Reuters in response to an inquiry.
Viag plans to swap its 50 percent share in Thyssengas GmbH for RWE's 25 percent holding in power producer Isarwerke GmbH.
The deal, originally proposed in May, would enable Viag unit Bayernwerk AG to secure a majority share of Isarwerke GmbH's parent Isar-Amperwerke AG.

Earlier this month, the German cartel office asked the Commission if it could rule on the deal's risk of creating an anti-competitive situation in German gas and electricity markets. The Commission agreed to this request earlier on Tuesday.
